teams.heading: Fiji lose four of last five fixtures following home defeat to Japan
teams.body: Fiji have registered just one victory in their last five fixtures. Across those same five games, the national team suffered four defeats. The most recent of those results came in September 2026, when they fell to a 20-15 home defeat against Japan. That match was played during the knockout stage of the Pacific Nations Cup, marking their fourth loss within that five-game window.

teams.heading: Henry Pollock emerges as leading option to replace injured Sam Underhill
teams.body: Following Sam Underhill's ruled-out status due to a ruptured bicep, Henry Pollock has emerged as a front-runner to step into England's starting back row for the November Tests. Steve Borthwick must reshuffle his loose forwards, with analysis positioning a balanced trio of Pollock, Ollie Chessum and Ben Earl as the leading combination. Pollock, regarded as a confidence player, could partner Earl and Chessum to share the carrying workload and provide a dynamic option for the national side's upcoming autumn campaign.

teams.heading: Saracens Appoint Brendan Venter To New 'Wine Consultant' Culture Role
teams.body: Saracens have resolved a long-running dispute regarding media non-attendance by appointing Brendan Venter as 'head of rugby culture and wine consultant.' The move follows the former Springbok's repeated failure to fulfil mandatory media duties, which previously led to disciplinary scrutiny and the threat of fines from Premiership Rugby. By reassigning Venter to this unconventional role, the club appears to be exploiting a loophole in league regulations to avoid further disciplinary action for future media absences.

teams.heading: Ireland Women host England at Aviva Stadium in 2027 tournament
teams.body: Ireland Women will face England at the Aviva Stadium in the fourth round of the 2027 Six Nations on 8 May. Scott Bemand’s side return to the Dublin venue following a successful debut there last year, which saw a record crowd of 31,294 attend their victory against Scotland. Captain Erin King noted the group’s excitement to return to the "home of Irish rugby" for the fixture, which follows a campaign that includes home matches against France in Galway.

lead.why: The announcement of a high-profile home fixture at the Aviva Stadium is a significant development for Irish rugby fans.

teams.heading: Henry Pollock signs multi-year Northampton Saints contract extension deal
teams.body: Northampton Saints have secured the future of Henry Pollock, with the England back-rower signing a new multi-year contract extension. While recent speculation had linked the player to a potential £1m-a-year salary, reports today indicate the actual value of his new deal exceeds £400k. The agreement concludes months of uncertainty regarding his club future, during which Pollock had previously denied signing terms and remained publicly open to alternative opportunities. He now remains at Franklin's Gardens on revised financial terms.

teams.heading: Les Kiss releases Tupou and Hooper for upcoming Bledisloe Cup series
teams.body: Head coach Les Kiss has confirmed his 34-man squad for the Bledisloe Cup, opting to release Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper as they return to their respective clubs. With the upcoming Tests sitting outside of World Rugby Regulation Nine, the pair will not feature against the All Blacks. Toby Macpherson earns a maiden call-up to bolster the forwards, while Massimo de Lutiis returns. "It’s pleasing to keep the core of our squad together," said Kiss regarding his selections.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby Football Union Confirms Bid For 2035 World Cup
teams.body: The Japan Rugby Football Union has officially launched a bid to host the Men's Rugby World Cup in 2035, aiming to bring the prestigious tournament back to Asia. Anchored by the core message of No Side Spirit, the campaign coincides with the JRFU's 100th anniversary celebration. The bid committee is organising a shortlist of eight to ten high-capacity stadiums accommodating at least 25,000 spectators to meet World Rugby's updated guidelines, leveraging the successful commercial momentum from the 2019 tournament.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie rejects rotation approach for upcoming Bledisloe Cup matches
teams.body: Dave Rennie has confirmed the All Blacks will give the Wallabies full respect in their upcoming Bledisloe Cup series by avoiding the heavy rotation seen elsewhere in international rugby. Unlike Springboks boss Rassie Erasmus, who made 13 changes for a recent outing, Rennie intends to pick his strongest possible squad as New Zealand look to bounce back from three successive defeats against South Africa. "We’re still big on earning the right to play and so the Bledisloe Cup matches are important to us," Rennie said.

teams.heading: Rob Baxter addresses Springbok's omission while Test star nears return
teams.body: Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter has insisted that hooker Joseph Dweba is not far away from a return after missing the opening two competitive fixtures of the season. Dweba, who boasts seven Test caps for South Africa, was overlooked for the opening PREM Rugby Cup victory over Bristol Bears and the defeat to Gloucester in favour of club stalwart Jack Yeandle and Louie Gulley. Baxter stated that Dweba is training well and that his opportunities will come shortly in a competitive hooker department.
